paper.title: Algorithm 799: Revolve, an implementation of checkpointing for the reverse or adjoint mode of computational differentiation
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 26(1), March 2000, pp. 19-45 (archive header: TRANS. MATH. SOFTWARE VOL. 26, NO. 1, March 2000, P. 19-45)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 799.gz (scouted 2026-11-27, gz sha256 8587175531d158f0c6f95f3bd507f149f04bbe0f1928810819c913d2c773a657; archive created 2000-09-04). Contains C/Src (revolve.h, src.c), C/Drivers (driver.c, data, res), Fortran77/Src (src.f), Fortran77/Drivers (driver.f, data, res), and Doc makefiles.

claim.location: Shipped reference output C/Drivers/res (sha256 1bb5a2b8c41c2552377e70f29dbd28c97a3490d91b74cdf05c9c36227de35e82). The driver reads STEPS=14, SNAPS=3, INFO=3 from C/Drivers/data, calls revolve() until terminate, and prints the action trace. The res file ends with 'advances: 27', 'takeshots: 6', 'commands: 47', and a header line 'slowdown factor: 1.9286' (27/14). The Fortran77/Drivers/res file gives the same counts.
claim.metric: Integer counts of forward advances, checkpoint takes and total commands for the optimal schedule with 14 steps and 3 snaps, plus the slowdown factor printed to 4 decimals. The full action trace in res is also checkable line by line.
claim.paper_value: Not located: the paper (ACM TOMS 26(1) 2000) is paywalled and was not read. The shipped res file is the value to check.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The three counts are integers from a deterministic schedule, so the tolerance is exact match (0). The slowdown factor is printed to 4 decimals, so its tolerance is half a printed unit (5e-5). Not loosened after any run. Caveat: the counts are the output of an optimal-schedule algorithm; the paper gives the binomial bound that such schedules meet, but the exact 27/6/47 trace is a computed value, not a closed form, so it tests the code.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: one schedule of 14 steps.
cost.data_size: Archive about 40 KB (1514 lines in the decompressed shell archive).
cost.data_licence: Not stated in the archive; a Collected Algorithm from ACM TOMS. The rerun should record the licence it finds.

why: The archive ships a driver that runs revolve() on a fixed input (14 steps, 3 snapshots) and a reference action trace, in both C and Fortran 77, so the schedule the code produces can be compared exactly with the shipped output.
